question: How dense are self-copying motifs among uniform random tapes of the frozen Z80 x Atlas byte substrate, what architectures exist, how often is access to exact self-copy gated by the environment's input byte, how robust are they to single-byte damage, and does the measured prior predict the campaign's 1 surviving random-origin world out of 27,141?
blindness: uniform random tapes from SplitMix64(seed_from('archaeon.copier_census.v1', stratum, chunk)); no search, selection, evolution or seeding. The 84616cf8257b founder tape and the hand-written replicators are RULERS (classifier controls), never templates. The engineering pilot used the separate 'PILOT-*' stream and is excluded from every estimate.
substrate: archaeon.z80atlas.vm.execute exactly as frozen at campaign commit c7610ea19 (vm.py unchanged since), empty neighbour window, single input byte x in 0..255, step_cap 256, non-metabolic, pc0 0 (shared layout)
phenotype_and_classes: archaeon/z80atlas/census/copier_census.py module docstring (birth = coverage >= 0.9; exact = birth and window == tape; span = longest single-offset run of written bytes equal to the tape; classes EXACT_UNGATED, EXACT_GATED, NEAR_COPIER, SPAN_COPIER, WRITER, TOUCH, INERT, first match wins)
instrument_gates_before_run: rulers: hand-written replicators (vmcopy, z80) -> EXACT_UNGATED; specimen founder -> EXACT_GATED at exactly input 121 with 26 birth inputs; all-NOP -> INERT
input-skip exactness: skipped sweep identical to a forced 256-input sweep on 300 tapes (both substrates)

stage2_per_hit.set: every hit of class SPAN_COPIER or better; if a stratum has more than 3000, a fixed-seed sample of 3000 (random.Random('stage2:'+stratum))
stage2_per_hit.offspring: the child window at the representative birth input is swept; heritable = child class is SPAN_COPIER or better
stage2_per_hit.damage: 32 positions x 8 distinct substitutions (seeded per tape) = 256 single-byte mutants; report fraction keeping class tier, any exact input, any birth; essential positions = positions where no substitution keeps any exact input
stage2_per_hit.occupied_neighbour: the tape re-executed at up to 16 of its exact (else representative) inputs against a seeded random neighbour window; births and exact copies counted

architecture_features: primitive (COPY / STORE / MIXED / NONE from executed opcodes), gating (ungated 256 / gated 2..255 / gated1 / no_exact), control (relative jump / absolute jump / straight), offset (k0 / shift), input use (reads_input / input_blind); families are tuples of these; no loop-matching against any known tape

prediction.model: lambda = sum over campaign random-init endogenous worlds w without inserted material of 1 - (1 - p_s)^F, F = N * init_fill_pct = 76.8 expected random founders; p_s = density of exact-capable tapes (EXACT_UNGATED + EXACT_GATED) in the world's (substrate, genome) stratum for worlds whose task supplies a uniform input byte, or density of tapes exact at input 0 for task=none worlds (whose IN reads 0). lambda = expected number of campaign worlds that contained at least one exact-capable copier founder; it is an UPPER bound on worlds a copier could have rescued.
prediction.interval: lambda recomputed at the Clopper-Pearson 95% bounds of each stratum density
prediction.observed: 1 surviving world of 27,141 (84616cf8257b_s1_cont, stratum vmcopy32, uniform input)

stop_conditions: any chunk errors (the chunk is rerun from its own seed; results never patched)
a class definition or threshold would need to change after results (-> COPIER-CENSUS-02)
